paragraphs.source_en: I often visited Kiyo after we had closed our house. Her nephew was a comparatively good man. He used to entertain me in more ways than one each time I called when he was at home. Kiyo was happy to have me come, and would tell him many fine things about me. Once she declared that I would purchase a fine residence somewhere in Kōjimachi and attend my office in a fine carriage. Being her own judge, she would talk on and on without consulting me, and thus I blushed often, being very much embarrassed. I bore this once or twice like a saint, but found it very hard to bear when she began to spin a yarn how I urinated in my sleep when a child. I do not know how her nephew felt about her proud talk of me, but Kiyo being a woman of the old school thought that her relation to me was that of a vassal to his lord at feudal times, and it was not at all strange logic for her to conclude that her nephew came under the same code.
